message: fix(progression): make the long-term mastery floor gradual rather than a terminal jump
purpose: Review correction before balance verification. Preserve the historic level mapping for old characters and the reduced credit for future awards, but approach the overall cap gradually as all skills approach mastery. Do not jump a character dozens of levels on the last XP point. Add an independent near-cap boundary test.

replacements.old: Test("Invalid awards fail before state changes and zero awards do not manufacture XP",()=>
All 60 skills at their cap retain the existing terminal overall-level milestone. The prior overall XP-to-level mapping runs on credited training rather than destructively recalculating past progress.
replacements.new: The prior overall XP-to-level mapping runs on credited training rather than destructively recalculating past progress. A gradual late-game mastery floor prevents a character from being stranded below the overall cap after all skills cap. With q = raw total skill XP / (60 * skill-cap XP), the floor is 1 + floor(199 * q^1.5). Overall level is the greater of that floor and the credited-XP level. This floor is negligible during early play and approaches level 200 continuously; it does not create a last-point jump. Trivial combat still earns only its reduced practice before it contributes to mastery.
